1.note: מַעֲלוֹת is "steps, ascents" and also "rank, excellence" (מַעֲלָתוֹ, "his rank", two lines on). The phrase plays on שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת, the "Song of Ascents" of the Psalms.

2.note: Literally "and splits brightnesses from his dawns": the poet breaks out like the light of dawn. The image is uncertain.

3.note: נְסוּכוֹת is "poured, cast" (as metal) or "set up, installed" (Prov 8:23 נִסַּכְתִּי). Read as "fixed".

4.note: The edition points אַדְנֵי, "the bases (sockets) of" (Job 38:6), not אֲדֹנִי, "my lord", which the unpointed letters also allow.

5.note: סְעִפַּי read as "my thoughts" (Job 4:13 סְעִפִּים; Ps 94:19 שַׂרְעַפַּי). Literally the word is "my branches".

6.note: In Exod 22:28 these are offerings: the first of the full harvest and of the juice of the press. The poem reads מְלֵאָה as the eye "full" of tears and דֶּמַע as "tears" (דִּמְעָה).

7.note: The author's own name is Judah (al-Ḥarizi). The verse may also be heard as "the Lord is the portion that Judah inherits".

8.note: A sound play: אֲלֻמּוֹת "sheaves", אִלְּמוּ "fell dumb", and אֲלֻמָּתִי "my sheaf" of Joseph's dream (Gen 37:7).

9.note: The meaning of פְּרָזָיו in Hab 3:14 is uncertain (warriors, leaders, or villagers). The envier is struck with his own weapons. The poem also plays on מַטֶּה (rod, here the pen) and מַטָּיו (his shafts).

10.note: Measure for measure: the beloved's eyes wounded the lover's heart, so the lover's eyes wound the beloved's cheeks, perhaps by making them blush. The sense is uncertain.

11.note: A rhyming pair: הוֹרֶה "parent" (the one who conceived you) and מוֹרֶה "teacher"; מוֹרָא is also "fear".

12.note: In Lev 20:14 "them" (feminine) are the women; here they are his lusts (תַּאֲוֹתָיו, feminine).

13.note: The edition points אֵידִי, "my calamity". A play on אֵד, "mist" (Gen 2:6), fits the image of tears that freeze. The sense is uncertain.

14.note: In Ps 147:18 God sends His word and melts the ice. Here the subject may be the fire of the heart, as translated, or God: "but He sends His word to the fire of my heart".

15.note: Literally "Your people, draw up from the sea, affliction, tossed". Read with Isa 57:20 כַּיָּם נִגְרָשׁ, "like the tossing sea". The syntax is uncertain.

16.note: The poem has וְעַל, the challenge line and Ps 50:3 have וְאַל, "and not". Translated as וְאַל.

17.note: A sound play (מַפְלִיא / פְלִילִיּוֹת). פְּלִילִיָּה is "judgment" (Isa 28:7). The sense, "who does wonders in judging", is uncertain.

18.note: Literally "my face was revealed": the gloom left it. It answers the old man's covered face ("His face was covered") and leads into the heavens that are rolled up (נָגֹלּוּ) in the next line.
